original_target.title: Is there a uniform polynomial bound for three commuting contractions?
original_target.area: Operator theory and multivariable functional calculus

scope_comparison: Arbitrary scalar polynomials, a fixed triple and arbitrary Hilbert-space dimension require a single finite K3. Hartz–Wang introduction still separates unknown C(3) from the homogeneous C(3,n) bounds; Kiri's October theorem has a matrix-size-dependent constant. Failure at constant one does not refute a finite unspecified constant.

primary_sources.locator: Introduction lines53–73; C(d), C(d,n) and homogenization inequality.

Palomar.scope: Routing only. Hexagon Hua–Bellman noncommuting-contraction determinant positivity is not the commuting-triple scalar polynomial bound.
